Corroboration: 1922 Tours Mame, printed p. 542 (artifact PDF p. 656), target-body character coverage 0.99, found by a sweep; Benziger 1962 conformed printing, target-body character coverage 0.94. The 1862 does not print these words under this day: they were found by sweeping that book end to end and stand at the locus given, under another day of the same book. An order is not a contribution, so the words are still a public-domain antecedent, but a reviewer should know the position differs. Every 1862 reading here rests on that book's whole-book text layer alone; this lane has no page image of the 1862, and the recogniser damages roughly one word in three there, so where the 1862's letterforms differ from the 1962's the difference recorded above is an inference from the layer and not a reading of the leaf. The 1922 Mame is the check on those places, and it is a full public-domain peer rather than mere corroboration. The verdict, the antecedent locus and the recorded differences are the original lane's and were not revisited. CORRECTION TO THE LOCUS: the stored locus named marginal no. 2247. propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Mysticis, Domine, repleti sumus votis et gaudiis: praesta, quaesumus; ut
intercessionibus sanctarum Martyrum tuarum Perpetuae et Felicitatis, quae
temporaliter agimus, spiritualiter consequamur. Per Dominum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n936, printed p. 938, under `Postcommunion` at the end of the Mass of Saints Perpetua and Felicity. The facing Latin is the 1962 slot's prayer, with both saints printed by name in both columns.
translations.source_label: The New Roman Missal in Latin and English, revised edition, by F. X. Lasance and Francis Augustine Walsh (New York: Benziger Brothers, 1945), ca. 1955-56 printing (Internet Archive delivery locator fr-lasance-missal-1937; locator mislabelled)
translations.text: Thou hast filled us, O Lord, with mystic graces and joys: grant, we beseech Thee, that through the prayers of Thy holy Martyrs, Perpetua and Felicitas, we may profit eternally from having in this our time ministered to Thee. Through our Lord.
